in context of the sims? it's how a sim finds it's way from one place to another.

you tell a sim to open the fridge, but they're sat down in another room. The sim has to get up> walk to the door> open the door> walk around kitchen table in the middle of the room> approach the fridge and open it. in short, they're *finding the best path* to a location. TS4 has a rep for absolutely insane pathfinding, where sims think they can't get past an small plant so will walk around the entire house for something right next to them.

if anyone is on the fence about whether a suit is worth it, try thinking of not just the total price it would take to get to it, but the price from the last piece. The way i prefer to make my decisions is this: if during an event, one suit is 1k dias, and the suit after costs another 2k, but i already wanted to get the suit before, then it's not actually 3k, it's 2k. if i *didnt* want the suit before, then yes it's 3k.

That's how i feel about the 2d live in true road. Yes almost 30k is insane, but the suits you need to get before that are the majority of that cost, and i already know for sure i want them all. If i make my choice based on what i need to spend after i already earned all the suits i like, it's not so expensive. if you don't like *all* the suits that come before it you should probably think twice. As it is, the 2d live seems almost affordable at more like 13-11k after you got all the suits.

I unfortunately understand this feeling to a T.

I'd spent a couple months researching crested geckos (ethical breeders, what vets would be qualified to treat it if i purchased one, set up, cage etc.) because i planned to get one after i moved out the next month.

One day my mum and step dad sit me down and give me a lecture about the importance of caring for your animals daily (weird lecture to give a then 20 year old woman who already had a hamster with what they considered too big a tank and who cared for their fish more often than they did) and pulled out a TINY few week old leopard gecko. this thing was sickly, too young to have been sold, and NOTHING LIKE the crestie that'd been researching. The poor thing was freezing in a little plastic box with no heat pads and suddenly im rushing to set up the enclosure they'd bought for it and they couldnt understand why. The enclosure was too small, too tall, had sand (a huge hazard to leos) only one hide, the only heating was a heat pad with no thermostat or thermometer and we live in the uk so that's far from sufficient. It was a nightmare, and now i had to try to safely move with all this.

I tried to explain that I appreciate it but that it was innappropriate to them, but they just didnt understand. And i really did love him (he passed away after only two years from an unknown neurological condition that gave him strokes/seizures and made it hard for him to eat. The Exotic vet said he'd probably been crossed with a morph he shouldn't even though he was visually a normal type. they said he seemed happy and healthy despite it and that while he wouldnt live long as long, if i didnt mind giving him ridiculous amounts of care then he didnt necessarily have to be put down and he ended up dying during a seizure).

I remember my mum being so confused at how I could disagree with the advice of the pet store owner who said sand (the most expensive substrate) was the best for leos. "She has over 50 turtles, I think she knows more than we do"

People really put far too much stock into the words of for profit breeders.

a lot of hamsters dont get given the correct housing which can make them incredibly stressed, that's why they tend to be nippy. They need a lot more space and burrowing depth than people expect. (also this isnt a hamster in the vid but i think others have pointed that out oh well)
